note: India's largest banks are the State Bank of India (whose cards SBI Card issues), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank. SBI Card is written here; HDFC Bank's and ICICI Bank's terms weren't reached in this pass. SBI Card's most important terms and conditions (read again 2026-10-30): every card in its fee table is written (the Vyapaar Unnati and SimplySAVE Merchant cards, for merchants, aren't), each with its one-time annual fee at issue (written as the issue fee; none where the table says NIL) and its renewal fee each year from the second, waived where the table states spending of a figure in the preceding year (a lakh is 100,000 rupees; the Bank of Maharashtra SimplySAVE renewal printed '4,99' is read as 499), the SBI Card Unnati's renewal fee from its fifth year (written as waived for four years); the SimplySAVE SBI Card this file has held since 2026-10-29 (499, waived on 1 lakh) is among them. Finance charges up to 3.75% a month (45% a year) on unsecured cards, written at that figure, and 2.75% a month on the Shaurya (defence) and secured cards (the PRIME NRI Secured), on purchases and cash; interest-free 20 to 50 days on purchases when the previous balance was paid in full, written as 50; a cash advance 2.5%, at least 500 rupees; the minimum payment 2% of the balance plus all GST, instalments, fees, charges and finance charges and any over-limit amount (written as 2% with the interest added; the fees aren't); over the limit 2.5% of the excess, at least 600 rupees; a dishonoured payment 2% of the payment, at least 500 rupees (written as 500); spending in another currency 3.5%, 3% on the MILES, 2.5% on the MILES PRIME and 1.99% on the AURUM, ELITE, PRIME NRI Secured, Tata Neu Infinity and MILES ELITE (read as the SBI Card ELITE and ELITE Advantage for 'Elite'; the partner banks' ELITE cards are written at 3.5%); GST at 18% on all fees, interest and charges (Haryana's 9% central and 9% state are the same 18%). The late payment charge is a step by the amount due (nothing up to 100 rupees, then 100, 500, 750, 950, 1,100 and 1,300 above 50,000, with 100 more after two missed cycles), which the form doesn't hold, so it isn't written; nor are the 250-rupee cash payment fee, the 1% utility, education and wallet fees above their thresholds, or the 99-rupee redemption fee.
